newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mogas touch stronger, wet tight.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mogas touch stronger, wet tight.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Monday with Brent CFDs narrowly weaker, gasoline marginally firmer and naphtha and fuel essentially flat.
Dealers said gasoline continued to be a powerful force in the energy complex with very tight wet supplies underpinning strength.
A eurograde loading today was sold at least $6 above a first half August loading, wet dealer said.
Gasoline swaps traded at $198.50 and $199.50 for August which was pegged at the close around $200. September remained backwardated by $7-8 and with the October/November spread put around $5-6.
Ready avails were not expected before mid August which should keep swaps firm.
Brent CFDs were weaker with July 28-August 1 put at +8 cents against September Brent from +12 cents on Friday while August 4-8 was -7 cents compared with -5 cents.
August 11-15 was pegged at -13 cents from -12 cents while August 18-22 was seen at -22/23 cents from -13 cents.
August 11-15 traded at September Brent -11 cents and July 28-August 1 went at +8 cents.

Heavy fuel essentially moved sideways for much of the day, gaining 50 cents then shedding 75 cents. Towards the close of the day heavy fuel August swaps were talked at $89.50-90 with September 50 cents or so stronger, prices very close to Friday's levels.
August traded at $89.50 and September went at $89.75 and $90.
Low sulphur swaps were marginally easier with August talked around $93.75-4 with September ranged between $95.50-96.
August naphtha started early in the morning at $188 before moving to $191 and then $190. Dealers said $191 and $190.75 and $190.50 were all done while September traded at $188.25.
